hazard.quote: FIGURE 1.3: Performance on autonomy tasks across three risk areas
hazard.note: The only AI-risk use of the word: 'precursors (skills upstream of hazardous capabilities)'. Never defined beyond this gloss.

hazard.quote: Wet lab: A laboratory designed for the handling of chemicals
hazard.note: Glossary; a different sense: physical/chemical 'wet' hazards in a lab. Of interest only as a sense of the word.

catastrophic risk.note: The phrase 'catastrophic risk' never appears. 'catastrophic' occurs once (line 476), qualifying loss of control as the worst case, with 'the severity of this outcome' as the reason it warrants attention. No thresholds or definition.

loss of control.note: Section 5 opening: the report's only framing of loss of control -- model-originated risk set against misuse, 'catastrophic, irreversible loss of control' as the worst case, and why self-replication and sandbagging are tracked.
First of the two loss-of-control capabilities: RepliBench results (<5% to >60%), early vs late stages, and the caveat that simplified tasks don't guarantee real-world ability.
Second capability: definition, induced sandbagging, detection methods and their decline, and no spontaneous sandbagging found in 2,700 transcripts.

loss of control.quote: Some of the capabilities that would be required for AI models to evade human control
loss of control.note: Executive summary of section 5; adds the 'reliably directed towards human goals' framing.

loss of control.quote: Loss of control: We track emerging capabilities such as self-replication
loss of control.note: Testing-approach list: loss of control as an evaluation domain.

loss of control.quote: FIGURE 1.3: Performance on autonomy tasks across three risk areas
loss of control.note: Simplified self-replication and AI R&D as autonomy risk areas; points to section 5.

humans can no longer shut down or correc.note: Closest the report comes: 'catastrophic, irreversible loss of control' and 'AI's ability to evade human control'. It never states loss of control in terms of shutting down or correcting a system.

humans can no longer shut down or correc.quote: Some of the capabilities that would be required for AI models to evade human control
humans can no longer shut down or correc.note: 'ensuring that increasingly autonomous systems are reliably directed towards human goals' -- a near-echo of the EU Code's 'reliably direct, modify, or shut down', without the shutdown/modify limbs.

humans can no longer shut down or correc.quote: To self-replicate in the real world, AI systems would need to complete several actions
humans can no longer shut down or correc.note: The concrete picture of evading control: acting 'while remaining undetected', 'maintaining persistent access' to compute.

misalignment.note: The word is never used. The concept appears as 'novel risks that emerge from models themselves behaving in unintended or unforeseen ways', set against misuse (line 474), with self-replication defined as acting 'without being explicitly prompted'.

misalignment.quote: We have yet to detect any instances of models intentionally sandbagging
misalignment.note: The report's evidence on spontaneous (unprompted) misbehaviour: none detected; some models noticed evaluation and 'acted differently'.

misalignment.quote: Some of the capabilities that would be required for AI models to evade human control
misalignment.note: 'reliably directed towards human goals'; 'not yet evidence of models attempting to sandbag or self-replicate spontaneously'.

misalignment.quote: As AI systems are increasingly integrated into society, the challenge is to anticipate
misalignment.note: The only use of 'aligned': near-term adoption 'aligned with human intent'.

serious incident.quote: People are increasingly turning to AI systems for emotional support
serious incident.note: No 'serious incident' or 'incident' anywhere. The nearest is 'recent high-profile cases of harm' (footnote 30, line 650: a teenager's death by suicide alleged against ChatGPT), cited as motivation for research, not as an incident in any reporting sense.

what must a developer publish or report.quote: During our testing, we are granted API access to model checkpoints
what must a developer publish or report.note: The report states no obligations. This is the only description of pre-release practice: AISI gets API access to checkpoints, sometimes ahead of public release or with different safeguards.

what must a developer publish or report.quote: The above is a subset of our chemistry and biology evaluations
what must a developer publish or report.note: Mentions 'labs' own risk thresholds' as something AISI assesses against -- the only nod to developers' own frameworks.

what must a developer publish or report.quote: Building consensus around AI risks and designing appropriate mitigations
what must a developer publish or report.note: Sandbagging could lead to 'models being released without proper safeguards' -- why pre-release evaluation matters, not what must be published.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Section 3's framing of the chem/bio risk: dual-use capabilities 'available to everyone, including those with harmful intentions'; 'barriers limiting risky research to trained specialists are eroding'.
Scope of the chem/bio evaluations; QA results beyond the PhD baseline (-0.4 in 2022 to +0.6 relative in 2025).

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: When equipped with tools like search or code execution, scaffolded AI agents
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Agents retrieving sequences for plasmid design; weeks to days; still fail end-to-end.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: Models can now consistently produce detailed and accurate protocols
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: The most direct uplift result: non-experts using frontier models had 4.7x odds (CI 2.8-7.9) of a feasible viral-recovery protocol vs internet alone; feasible protocols since late 2024, wet-lab verified.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: In addition to testing how well models write protocols, we also test their ability
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Troubleshooting: every frontier model beats experts; novices succeed at hard wet-lab tasks with an LLM.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: Models can combine vision capabilities with advanced knowledge and reasoning
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Multimodal troubleshooting from images beats experts from mid-2025, widening access for non-experts.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: The above is a subset of our chemistry and biology evaluations
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Other misuse-risk evaluations exist (undisclosed); assessment against labs' own risk thresholds.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: We've partnered with the top AI companies to stress-test their safeguards
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Universal jailbreaks extracted answers to biological misuse requests; 10 minutes vs over seven hours, six months apart.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: Some AI systems are much more robust to some categories of malicious requests
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Biological misuse is the best-defended category; others are easier to jailbreak.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: As AI capabilities continue to advance across domains, malicious actors
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: The only occurrence of 'weapons' in the report ('aid in weapons development').

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: In chemistry and biology, AI models have far surpassed PhD-level experts
Human uplift studies that assess real-world utility of AI systems
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: How the report measures uplift; glossary definition at line 832 adds the internet-only control group.

chemical and biological weapons uplift.quote: Human uplift study: A study designed to measure the helpfulness of AI models
chemical and biological weapons uplift.note: Glossary definition of the uplift method.

evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.note: Definition; models can tell test from deployment; induced sandbagging that fools automated monitors; AISI confirms subtle induced sandbagging even in older open-weight models.

evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.quote: We have some methods for detecting sandbagging, but they may become less effective
evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.note: Black-box monitors and white-box deception probes; accuracy falls on larger models and agentic tasks; harder to detect when trained to imitate weaker models.

evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.quote: We have yet to detect any instances of models intentionally sandbagging
evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.note: No spontaneous sandbagging in 2,700+ transcripts; a few cases of models noticing evaluation and acting differently; can't rule out undetectable sandbagging.
Why these capabilities are tracked: prerequisites for evading human control.
Self-replication capability, including staying undetected and keeping persistent access; no sabotage evidence as such.

evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.quote: Some of the capabilities that would be required for AI models to evade human control
evidence that models can sabotage, sandb.note: Summary: sandbag when prompted; no evidence of spontaneous sandbagging or self-replication.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Dual-use framing; apprentice-level from <9% to 50%; first model completing expert-level tasks in 2025.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.quote: Enhanced access to tools, via better model scaffolding, consistently improves
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Enhanced scaffolding +9.8 points on the dev set; evaluations may underestimate the ceiling; 13% of the token budget for the same performance.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.quote: Frontier AI models still struggle to complete realistic, step-by-step cyber challenges
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Cyber range: early flags increasingly solved, later flags rarely.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.quote: This trend is reflected in other domains we test as well
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Lives in section 2 (Agents), not 3.2: cyber task length from <10 min to >1 hour, doubling about every eight months (an estimated upper bound).

cyber capabilities of frontier models.quote: Progress in the cyber domain is also significant
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Section 3 summary of cyber progress and examples of tested skills.

Task difficulty level (TDL): Our framework for assessing the difficulty
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Defines the apprentice/practitioner/expert levels the cyber claims are stated in.

cyber capabilities of frontier models.quote: We may be underestimating the ceiling of capabilities, particularly in adversarial
cyber capabilities of frontier models.note: Limitation bearing on cyber claims: no fine-tuning access, no maximised inference compute.

how the severity or acceptability of a r.note: The report decides nothing about acceptability. Its one severity argument: loss of control is uncertain, but 'the severity of this outcome means it warrants close attention'.

how the severity or acceptability of a r.note: Implicit stance on residual risk: misuse can't be eliminated; the 'adaptation buffer' reduces its 'scale and severity'.
